title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Game plan in three phases

Build the archive (turns 1–3): surveil with Gorehound, Glarb, Risky Research, and the surveil lands. Let burn spells hit the graveyard naturally or through Traumatic Critique’s “draw two, discard one”. Keep the board with early burn and Prismari Charm.
Light the flame (turns 4–6): resolve Iroh, Grand Lotus. Attack with Firebending creatures (Fire Lord Azula, Sun Warriors, Iroh himself) to stockpile red mana. Cast flashback burn from the yard — Azula copies it while she attacks.
Burn the library down: loop the flashback chain each turn, escalate with Firebender Ascension (copying Azula’s copy trigger), Sozin's Comet (firebending 5 on every creature), and Ozai (unspent mana becomes red). Shimmercreep and Explosive Prodigy add on-entry damage; Vivid beatdown closes games where burn stalls.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Curve and mana
24 lands: 18 nonbasic fixing/utility lands plus 7 basics (2 Forest, 2 Swamp, 1 Island, 1 Mountain, 1 Plains). The manabase is the deck’s Vivid engine — five colors among permanents means every Vivid X equals 5, so fixing lands are payoff lands. Mirage Mesa and Jasmine Dragon Tea Shop (for the Ally engine) smooth the five-color demands; Bloom Tender and Training Compound accelerate into Iroh on turn 4.
The nonland curve is 2 one-drops, 6 twos, 5 threes, 10 fours, 6 fives, 5 sixes, 2 seven-plus — an average mana value under 3. The deck plays most of its burn at one or two mana and leans on Iroh (5) and Ozai (6) as the top end.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Early game (turns 1–3)

Turn 1: Snarling Gorehound (every subsequent small creature surveils 1) or Burst Lightning for an early blocker. Surveil aggressively — the graveyard is the deck’s second hand.
Turn 2: Glarb, Calamity’s Augur (tap to surveil 2, and it casts your four- and five-drops from the top), Risky Research (surveil 2, draw two), or burn. Explosive Prodigy on turn 2 deals 3-4 damage to a creature and adds red to the color count.
Hold Prismari Charm or Unsubtle Mockery for the turn-2/3 threat. Discard lands or redundant burn to Traumatic Critique’s loot — the archive wants them.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Mid game (turns 4–6)

Resolve Iroh, Grand Lotus as the priority. With Glarb out, cast it from the top of the library. With Bloom Tender or a five-color board, it comes down on turn 4.
Once Iroh is down, the flashback suite is live: Burst Lightning for {R}, Firebending Lesson for {1}, Traumatic Critique for {X}{U}{R}. Attack with Firebending creatures first, generate red, then cast during combat while the mana is available.
Fire Lord Azula attacks with firebending 2, and every spell cast while she attacks is copied — a kicked Burst Lightning becomes 8 damage. Protect her with removal and Prismari Charm bounce.
Firebender Ascension accumulates quest counters every time an attacking creature triggers (Azula’s copy trigger, every Firebending trigger). At four counters it copies those abilities — Azula’s trigger copies twice, Firebending mana doubles.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
The combo turn

Confirm Iroh is on the battlefield and the archive holds at least two or three burn spells (surveil lands, Glarb, and Traumatic Critique’s loot keep it stocked).
Enter combat. Attack with Fire Lord Azula and Iroh (firebending 2 each), ideally with Sozin's Comet cast first (firebending 5 on everything) or Fire Nation Palace activated ({1}{R}, {T}) to grant firebending 4 — an Iroh with both printed firebending 2 and the Palace’s firebending 4 generates 6 red mana per attack.
With the combat mana banked, cast from the graveyard: Burst Lightning, Firebending Lesson, Traumatic Critique with X as high as the mana allows. Azula copies each spell; with Firebender Ascension at four quest counters, the copy trigger itself is copied.
Repeat each turn. Shimmercreep and Explosive Prodigy add on-entry damage, Ozai turns leftover mana red and becomes an indestructible flyer at six-plus unspent mana, and the loop outpaces any removal that isn’t graveyard hate.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Win condition 2: the Vivid beatdown
Burn is plan A; the board is plan B. Squawkroaster is a double striker whose power equals the number of colors among permanents you control — 5 or more in this deck, so it attacks as a 5/5 double strike minimum. Glister Bairn makes it +X/+X bigger every combat, and Prismabasher-style team pumps come from the same Vivid scaling. Self-Destruct turns a pumped Squawkroaster into a one-shot fireball (it deals damage equal to its power to any target), and Ozai — trample, haste, firebending 4, flying and indestructible at six-plus unspent mana — closes the game alone. Shimmercreep’s life drain also wins without ever attacking.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Mulligan guide

Keep: 2–3 lands covering red plus one other color, a surveil source (Glarb, Gorehound, Risky Research) or early burn, and a path to Iroh by turn 5.
Trim: 5+ land hands, single-color hands, and hands with only the top end (Ozai, Sozin’s Comet, multiple Traumatic Critiques) and no early play.
The deck is happy to trade card quantity for quality: Traumatic Critique, Glarb, and the surveil lands all convert surplus cards into archive fuel.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Multiple Firebending instances stack. A creature with firebending 2 (Iroh) that gains firebending 4 from Fire Nation Palace triggers twice: 6 red mana per attack. Sozin’s Comet on top makes it 9.
Firebending mana lasts until end of combat — cast the flashback burn during the declare-attackers step while the mana is available. Iroh’s flashback works any time during your turn.
Iroh’s flashback is only during your turn, and each cast exiles the card after resolution — the loop is per-turn, not infinite. Multiple copies of a burn spell in the yard extend the chain.
Firebender Ascension copies attacking-creature triggered abilities — Azula’s spell-copy trigger and every Firebending mana trigger qualify. It does not copy static abilities.
Traumatic Critique’s loot is a feature: discarding burn into the archive sets up next turn’s flashback chain.
Glarb casts MV 4+ spells from the top — Iroh, Ozai, Squawkroaster, and Shimmercreep all qualify; surveil first to put the right card on top.
Ozai’s mana conversion means unspent Firebending red, treasure from Flick a Coin-style effects, and other colors all become red, letting one combat’s mana cast any mix of flashback spells.
Graveyard hate is the deck’s Achilles heel — versus heavy exile, pivot to the Vivid beatdown plan (Squawkroaster, Ozai) and stop over-investing in the archive.

title: Kindle the Archive
text:
Matchups

Aggro: early burn clears the board; Explosive Prodigy and Shimmercreep trade life-for-life favorably; Ozai becomes an indestructible wall at six unspent mana. Surveil toward removal first, engine second.
Control: the flashback loop is card-advantage-proof — every burn spell is a reusable threat, and counterspells only delay it. Glarb’s top-of-library casting dodges hand disruption. Fire Nation Palace’s firebending grant is instant-speed and uncounterable.
Midrange: race their threats with copied burn; Azula plus a stocked archive out-damages most midrange clocks. Squawkroaster beats blockers with double strike.
Graveyard hate (Rest in Peace-style): swap to plan B — Squawkroaster plus Self-Destruct and Ozai beatdown; keep surveil minimal and use the Vivid creatures as the primary threat.

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Game plan in three phases

Dig and disrupt (turns 1-3): Bilbo (draw a card) or Elvenking’s Harper on turn two, Crude Bent Blade to force a sacrifice, Pinecone Strike or Enchanted River’s Grasp to answer threats. Play Pit of Offerings early — its exile trigger grows the Army the moment Along the Crooked Way is online, and it fixes black/red/blue.
Turn on the engine (turns 4-5): Along the Crooked Way on curve, then Misty Mountains Raider. Every Edgewall Inn activation, every Pit of Offerings, every adventure cast and every dying creature card that leaves the yard stacks +1/+1 counters on the Army. Gundabad Opportunist and Bilbo keep cards flowing.
The kill or the heist (turns 6+): make the Army unblockable with Elvenking’s Harper and smash with Smaug’s Fury (first strike, +3/+0) — or counter their finisher with Thranduil’s Decree and cast it yourself, and Supper for Spiders on their turn after a board wipe steals everything.

Pit of Offerings

Edgewall Inn
Engine land — {3}, {T}, sacrifice: return an Adventure card from your graveyard to hand, triggering amass and re-buying Bilbo, Gollum or Lake-town Mariners; taps for a colour of your choice

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Curve and mana
22 lands over a 38-card spell base. The deck is dense at two and three mana (26 cards) so it can interact and set up the engine before the Army takes over. Pit of Offerings is the fixing lynchpin — it reliably taps for black, red or blue once it has exiled one card of each colour, and Edgewall Inn covers the awkward third colour. The top end (Thranduil’s Decree, Gandalf, Lake-town Mariners) is deliberately thin: five six-mana cards that each end a game on their own rather than a durdle pile.

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Early game (turns 1-3)
Curve Bilbo into Along the Crooked Way, or Harper into removal. Play Pit of Offerings on turn one or two even though it enters tapped — the exile trigger is an amass engine waiting to happen, and the fixing matters more than the tempo loss. Use Pinecone Strike and Enchanted River’s Grasp to keep the board clean while the Army is still 0/0. Do not trade your Army unless it saves the game — every +1/+1 counter on it is the win condition.

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Mid game (turns 4-6)
Land Along the Crooked Way and Misty Mountains Raider. The loop is: attack (amass 2), activate Edgewall Inn on a dead Bilbo or Gollum (amass 1 + card back), cast the adventure from hand, and watch the Army swell. Supper for Spiders shines after any board wipe or bad block — every creature that died this turn, from either side, becomes your Food. Crude Bent Blade’s forced sacrifice also feeds it.

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
The combo turn

Have Along the Crooked Way and a 4+ power Army on board (two attacks from Misty Mountains Raider plus one Pit of Offerings trigger usually suffice).
First main phase: {4}{U} on Elvenking’s Harper — the Army can’t be blocked this turn.
Smaug’s Fury on the Army: +3/+0, first strike, reach.
Attack with an unblockable, first-striking Army for lethal. Against menace math, Along the Crooked Way’s {1}{B} also makes it require two blockers — the Harper activation is the clean kill, menace is the fallback.

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Win condition 2 — the heist
When the Army is answered, steal the game instead:

Thranduil’s Decree counters any spell — and if it’s a permanent, exiles it and lets you cast it without paying its mana cost. Counter their board wipe, then play their bomb.
Supper for Spiders is a one-sided Reanimate for the turn: after combat or a wipe, their entire dead board comes to your side as Food (lose all other types) — you gain 3 life per sacrifice and they lose the recursion value.
Gundabad Opportunist exiles your own top card on entry — free card advantage that plays around hand disruption.
Lake-town Mariners is a 6/5 vigilance ward 2 that ends the game in three swings, and its Gone Fishing adventure flickers the Army to dodge removal and re-trigger nothing (counters stay — it’s a new object, so use it to save, not to buff).

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Mulligan guide
Keep: any hand with Along the Crooked Way or Misty Mountains Raider plus 3 lands; Pit of Offerings + Edgewall Inn hands fix everything; Bilbo hands draw into the engine. Mulligan: no lands, 5+ lands with no engine, or hands whose only coloured sources are tapped Pit of Offerings with no way to curve into black/red/blue. The deck can win without the engine — Supper for Spiders and Thranduil’s Decree are game-swingers on their own — but the Army is the fastest clock.

title: Thieves of the Crooked Way
text:
Key interactions and edge cases

Pit of Offerings targets any graveyards: exile creature cards from your own yard to grow the Army, or strip a key card from your opponent’s yard — both modes trigger nothing for them and everything for you.
Edgewall Inn only returns Adventure cards: Bilbo, Gollum and Lake-town Mariners are the targets. Cast the adventure half from hand first, let the creature die, then re-buy the whole card.
Along the Crooked Way’s ETB itself amasses: returning a creature card from your graveyard to hand counts as a creature card leaving the graveyard, so the enchantment enters with at least one amass trigger.
The Army is a Goblin: it triggers the menace from Along the Crooked Way’s {1}{B} ability and is also an Orc-compatible Goblin — Misty Mountains Raider’s amass 2 finds it automatically.
Supper for Spiders is instant-speed: cast it in response to exile removal on your side of the board — it only grabs creatures “put there from the battlefield this turn”, so the window is the whole turn.
Thranduil’s Decree exiles only permanent spells: countering an instant or sorcery sends it to the graveyard normally — still a clean counterspell.
Enchanted River’s Grasp removes counters: it is the one card that shrinks an opposing Army — keep it for mirror matches and huge threats, not random attackers.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Overview
The Rewritten Stampede fuses three mechanics into one engine: Saddle mounts attack for value, Convoke spells are cast by tapping the same creatures, and Plan enchantments count every tap. The heart of the deck is Rewrite History: whenever one or more creatures you control become tapped, you draw a card, discard a card, and advance the plan. Attacking, saddling, convoking, and even Station all tap creatures — so every axis of the deck draws cards.
The other two Plans turn the same actions into resources. Death to Our Enemies makes a Treasure for every noncreature spell you cast (all your Convoke spells), which ramps the deck into its 5-6 mana finishers, and caps at 7 damage. Political Triumph turns every creature that enters into scry 1 plus a plan counter, ending in a global +1/+1 anthem.
The payoff is a go-wide Mount army. Seraphic Steed mints 3/3 flying Angels each saddled attack, Bridled Bighorn adds Sheep, Bounding Felidar pumps the whole team, Drover Grizzly gives trample, and Collective Inferno doubles all damage dealt by Mounts. Dracosaur Auxiliary swings in the air with haste and shocks anything. Games end in one massive, doubled, trampling stampede — or a 7-point burn finish.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Approach

Game plan phases

Setup (T1-3): Play Political Triumph or a cheap Mount (Gilded Ghoda, Seraphic Steed). Untap the Roads lands with a Mount in play and land Rewrite History.
Engine (T3-5): Resolve Rewrite History and Death to Our Enemies. Every saddle tap draws a card; every Convoke spell makes a Treasure. Mounts attack while saddled to generate tokens and Treasures.
Stampede (T5-7): Slam Collective Inferno (choose Mount), saddle Dracosaur Auxiliary / Bounding Felidar / Guardian Sunmare with Pilots and tokens, and attack for doubled, trampling, lifelink damage.
Cleanup: Burn with Death to Our Enemies (7 split), or bury the opponent in cards with Harmonized Crescendo (draw per Mount) and Rewrite History recursion.

Curve and mana
Average nonland CMC is 3.5. The curve peaks at 3-5; the two 6-drops (Dracosaur Auxiliary, Harmonized Crescendo) are effectively cheaper thanks to Convoke, Treasures, and Bucolic Ranch. The deck runs 23 lands but plays like 26: Treasures from Gilded Ghoda and Death to Our Enemies, plus creature-tapping for Convoke, generate the extra mana.

title: The Rewritten Stampede
text:
Gameplay strategy

Early game
Mulligan for Rewrite History plus any 1-2 drop Mount or Political Triumph. A turn-1 Political Triumph followed by creatures scries every draw step. Gilded Ghoda is the best early Mount: 2/2, saddle 1, and every saddled attack makes a Treasure — ramp and card draw on one body. Seraphic Steed (2/2 first strike, lifelink) races aggro while it waits for saddle 4.


Mid game
Land Death to Our Enemies and start casting Convoke spells — each one makes a Treasure. Unswerving Sloth is the engine-breaker: saddle it (tap 4 power), attack, and it untaps every creature you control, setting up a free main-phase Convoke turn. Guardian Sunmare tutors any nonland permanent with mana value 3 or less on a saddled attack — fetch a second copy of a Plan, another Mount, or a Convoke spell.


The combo turn

Have a wide board of Mounts and at least Collective Inferno (Mount).
Main phase 1: tap Pilots and tokens to saddle Dracosaur Auxiliary (saddle 3), Bounding Felidar (saddle 2) and Guardian Sunmare (saddle 4). Every tap draws a card off Rewrite History and every noncreature spell cast so far made a Treasure.
Attack: Dracosaur flies over for 4 (8 with Inferno) plus 2-4 shock damage; Felidar puts a +1/+1 counter on every other creature and gains life; Drover Grizzly grants trample; Seraphic Steed mints 3/3 Angels; lifelink keeps you ahead.
Main phase 2: Harmonized Crescendo (choose Mount) draws a card per Mount permanent — routinely 8-12 cards — or Unexpected Assistance digs deeper. Rewrite History then returns the best instants/sorceries from the graveyard to hand for the next loop.

A fully developed board deals 25-40 doubled, trampling damage in one swing.


Win condition 2: burn and grind
Death to Our Enemies reaches four plan counters after four noncreature spells (Plans, Convoke spells, and lands’ activated abilities do not count — spells only). That is easy with this shell: the payoff is 7 damage split as you choose, usually 7 to the face to finish after one stampede. In grindy games, Rewrite History recurs Temporal Cleansing, Appeal to Eirdu, and Unexpected Assistance, while Harmonized Crescendo refills the hand off the Mount count.


Mulligan guide
Keep: any hand with Rewrite History or Political Triumph plus 2-3 lands and a creature. Keep 2-land hands only with a 1-2 drop Mount (Gilded Ghoda, Seraphic Steed). Ship: hands without a Mount or a Plan, and hands flooded with 5-6 mana spells. Bucolic Ranch is a strong keep — it fixes and finds the finishers.


Key interactions and edge cases

Rewrite History triggers on any tap: attacking, saddling, convoking, and Station taps all draw. Plan the order — saddle first, then convoke, so each tap draws.
Pilots saddle as power 3: one Pilot covers saddle 1-3; two Pilots cover saddle 4 (Seraphic Steed, Guardian Sunmare, Unswerving Sloth).
The Wandering Rescuer protects tapped creatures with hexproof and blocks with flash, double strike — cast it with Convoke at instant speed.
Temporal Cleansing answers anything nonland, including indestructible threats (it tucks instead of destroying).
Adagia copies an enchantment at 12+ charge counters: copying Collective Inferno quadruples Mount damage; copying a Plan re-runs its payoff.
Death to Our Enemies cares about spells, not abilities: saddling and Station do not advance it, Convoke spells and Plans do.



Matchups

Aggro: Seraphic Steed’s lifelink, The Wandering Rescuer’s flash blocks, and Bounding Felidar’s lifegain stabilize; stall until the stampede.
Control: Death to Our Enemies ramps you through counterspells (Treasures are instant-speed mana), Rewrite History restocks after board wipes, and hexproof from The Wandering Rescuer protects tapped attackers.
Midrange: out-muscle with Angels, trample, and doubled damage; Temporal Cleansing removes the single biggest blocker.
